evidence.quote: So for now, I believe a pause in rate cuts is appropriate.
But if 2025 plays out like 2024, rate cuts would be appropriate at some point this year.
inflation is still meaningfully above our target, and progress has been excruciatingly slow over the last year.
The labor market is balanced and remarkably resilient.

My baseline view is that any imposition of tariffs will only modestly increase prices and in a non-persistent manner. So I favor looking through these effects when setting monetary policy to the best of our ability.
Whichever case it may be, the data are not supporting a reduction in the policy rate at this time.

parsed.rationale: Waller favors pausing cuts because inflation progress has stalled and the economy is strong, a mild hawkish lean. He still expects cuts later this year if inflation follows the 2024 pattern and plans to look through tariff effects, so the net signal is roughly balanced with a slight hawkish tilt.
